Past analyses of AAPL (most recent first):

[2026-10-01 | AAPL | Overweight | +3.1% | +1.8% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Overweight AAPL, but do not pay for the full overweight before the late-October 10-K. Keep the core; if the caller is below standard AAPL weight, add only half of the proposed first tranche (~0.12-0.20% of portfolio) after AAPL tests 322-324 and stabilizes above the 50 SMA/61.8% retracement, with a hard closing stop at 316.8 and a no-add/reduce warning on a >50M-share close below 322.18. Cap total exposure at roughly 110% of standard allocation pre-10-K, use a >50M-share close above 335.30 as an add-on trigger, and release later tranches only after the 10-K confirms gross margin at/above 48-49% with inventory converting and after a sustained break above 341.07. Target 345.34 over 1-3 months.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction belongs to the bull case; the timing and sizing belong to the bear and neutral cases. The aggressive analyst is right that AAPL is not a broken franchise and that the primary trend remains intact: 9M FY2026 revenue grew 16.1% to $364.4B, Q3 revenue grew 16.4%, gross profit grew 25.3%, operating income grew 26.6%, EPS grew 28.7%, and Q3 gross margin reached 50.06% while 9M gross margin expanded 225 bps to 49.07% even with R&D up 32.5%. Net cash rose $22.5B to $64.2B, term debt fell $8.3B, and price remains above a rising 50 SMA at 322.18 and 200 SMA at 288.86 with a widening golden cross. The pullback has come on 36.3M shares versus 70.0M on 9/10 and 86.6M on 9/18, which is more consistent with digestion than distribution. That evidence rules out Hold or Sell and supports owning AAPL.

But the conservative and neutral analysts win the execution argument. At 330.32, AAPL is below the 10 EMA at 333.70, VWMA at 335.30, and Bollinger mid-band at 331.62, MACD has crossed down, and the 331-336 shelf is overhead resistance. A blind 323.5 limit is only ~2% below spot and would buy while the short-term tape is still deteriorating; the 316.8 stop is 6.7 points from entry, less than one ATR of 7.25, and AAPL has already printed -8.58%/-7.36% on 2026-07-31, -6.12% on 6/25, and -5.0% on 2/12. Stops do not protect against gaps; size does. The 10-K is also a known binary event, the last filing was 2026-07-31, and the durability of the 50% gross-margin level is unproven against forward memory-cost pressure. Inventory is +94%, raw materials +260%, finished goods -4.1%, intangibles +91%, other noncurrent liabilities +32.5%, R&D +32.5%, and buybacks slowed 12%—items that could support the product-cycle thesis but are not yet proof of demand.

The neutral construction therefore governs: retain the Overweight bias but make the first tranche conditional and half-sized, requiring stabilization at 322-324 rather than catching a falling knife; treat a close below 322.18 on >50M shares as a warning to stop adding and consider reducing, keep 316.8 as the hard closing stop, cap pre-10-K exposure near 110% of standard rather than 125%, and hold the larger adds for the 10-K gross-margin/inventory gate and a sustained break above 341.07. This avoids both errors in the record: the repeated cost of under-owning AAPL inside an intact uptrend, and the flat-alpha outcome from sizing above benchmark into extended, unconfirmed price. Upgrade toward Buy on a 10-K with gross margin at/above 49.5%, inventory converting, buybacks re-accelerating, and a high-volume close above 341.07/345.34. Downgrade toward Hold/Underweight on a >50M-share close below 322.18, a close below 316.8, a 10-K gross margin below 48%, an inventory write-down, or deteriorating demand. Stated gaps: no sentiment report, no options chain or implied volatility, no segment/product/unit data, and no portfolio context, so all sizing must be scaled to the caller's own standard AAPL allocation.

**Price Target**: 345.34

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October 10-K

REFLECTION:
The +1.8% five-day alpha supports the Overweight directional call, but the window is far too short to validate a 1–3 month thesis or the 345.34 target. It supports the bull-case claim that AAPL’s primary uptrend was intact and that under-owning was the larger risk, while leaving untested the 322–324 stabilization, 335.30 VWMA reclaim, and 10-K gross-margin/inventory gates that governed sizing. Next time, tie the review window to the stated catalyst and predefine a short-horizon check—such as holding 322.18 and closing above 335.30—so a five-day alpha print is not mistaken for validation of a staged, event-gated plan.

[2026-09-30 | AAPL | Hold | +1.1% | -0.8% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Hold

**Executive Summary**: Hold AAPL: maintain the existing position at 0.75x–1.00x standard weight and place no new money at 333.02, which sits below the 10-EMA (334.45) and VWMA (335.34) for a second session with MACD 4.72 under its 5.32 signal and a 339.50 spike-and-fade on 49.99M shares still unresolved. Hard-cap exposure at 1.00x standard weight until the late-October FQ4/FY2026 print — not the 1.25x originally contemplated — because ATR is rising (6.83→7.25) and AAPL has already gapped −7.36% on 132.5M shares on 31 July, so size, not a closing stop, is the only real gap control. Stage any adds in three equal, evidence-gated tranches: a half-size probe only on two consecutive daily closes above 335.34 with no close back below 331.35, then a daily close above 339.50 on ≥50M shares with a held retest of 335.34, and the final third only after FQ4 clears gross margin ≥49.5%, revenue growth ≥15%, sequential inventory decline, tax ≤18%, and 10-K clarity on the ~$13B intangible/liability and its amortization terms. Risk ladder is closing-basis only: a close below 328.35 halts adds and forces a mandatory review, a close below 322.09 cuts to 0.5x standard weight, and a close below 316.27 exits to token/zero; if the position is above 1.00x, trim to the cap or buy a put/collar spanning the print rather than abandoning the core.

**Investment Thesis**: All three risk seats, the Research Manager and the trader land on Hold for AAPL, and here that is convergence rather than a shrug — the disagreement is only about the add ladder and the pre-print cap, and the bullish and bearish legs are genuinely symmetric at 333.02.

What the bullish case wins, and nobody rebutted it with a number: AAPL is not a broken franchise and the primary trend is up. Close 333.02 sits above a rising 50-SMA at 322.09 and a rising 200-SMA at 288.60, 15.4% above the 200-SMA with the 50-SMA 11.6% above the 200-SMA and widening, and 31 consecutive closes above the 50-SMA. Fundamentals are accelerating, not decaying: 9M revenue +16.1%, FQ3 revenue +16.4%, FQ3 gross margin 50.06% (+357 bps), FQ3 EPS +28.7%, 9M FCF $110.2B, net cash $62.2B with debt down 14.6%, and buybacks re-accelerated to $25.1B in FQ3 from $12.3B in FQ2. The bear produced no realized deterioration — no margin compression, no revenue loss, no unit weakness. That is why neither Underweight nor Sell survives: the conservative seat's own framing is "AAPL is not broken," and it conceded the franchise and the trend outright.

What the bearish case wins, and the bull conceded it twice: the entry is bad and the cash-flow headline is flattered. Roughly 45% of the 9M operating-cash-flow increase came from ~$15.8B of working-capital normalization, so underlying FCF growth is closer to 20% than 52.5%. The tape is deteriorating on the bull's own terms — close below the 10-EMA (334.45) and VWMA (335.34) for a second session, MACD 4.72 vs 5.32 signal with the histogram at −0.60 and widening after peaking at +2.03 on 3 September against a higher price high on 22 September, RSI 54.37 with no oversold cushion, and a 30 September candle that ran to 339.50 and closed 333.02 in the lower third of the range on 49.99M shares (~1.17x the September average). Upside is only ~0.7% to 335.34, ~2.0% to 339.50 and ~3.7% to the 345.34 record against ~3.3% to the 50-SMA. The quality-of-earnings caveats are real and quantified enough to gate adds: effective tax 17.58% from 15.39% with a ~27% incremental rate, inventory +94% to $11.1B with raw materials +260% (pre-build or write-down — genuinely two-sided), an unexplained ~$13B intangible matched by a non-current liability, ~36–37x an illustrative ~$9.1 FY2026 EPS midpoint with the 30-year yield at its highest since 2002, net cash only ~1.3% of a ~$4.86T market cap, and capital returns at 67% of FCF from 114%.

Where each seat overreaches, and how that fixes the size. The aggressive seat is right that the trend and franchise argue for ownership but wrong to pre-commit tranches above 335.34 and 339.50 before the FQ4 binary; its own first trigger is only ~0.7% above spot and below the unresolved rejection high, which is not evidence-gating, it is chasing a contested range into an event. The conservative seat is right that 322.09 is not a guaranteed fill — the 31 July −7.36% gap on 132.5M shares and a 30 September true range of 9.36 points (1.29x ATR) prove a closing stop is a marker, not protection — but capping at 0.75x and deferring every add until after FQ4 converts a genuine uncertainty into paralysis, and exiting to zero on a single close below 322.09 is too binary when 322.09 is only one-to-two ATR sessions away. The neutral construction therefore governs: hold the core, cap at 1.00x (not 1.25x, given gap risk), require stronger confirmation than a lone VWMA reclaim, and let FQ4 and the 10-K earn the next tranche. That cap is also what this desk's own record demands — the 09-23 Overweight at 337.02 produced −0.5% five-day alpha and its reflection concluded the first tranche should have been a probe sized for a pullback with volume confirmation required before the second, and the 09-22 Underweight at 339.75 earned +1.9% alpha precisely because a tool-verified momentum divergence at the top of the range was respected instead of discounted.

What would change the call, in both directions: upgrade to Overweight on a daily close above 339.50 on ≥50M shares with a held retest of 335.34, or on FQ4 gross margin ≥49.5% with inventory down sequentially, revenue growth ≥15%, tax ≤18% and a credible 10-K explanation of the ~$13B item (terms, amortization life, future cash payments); downgrade to Underweight on a daily close below 322.09 with the add schedule halted, and toward Sell on a close below 316.27, an inventory write-down, an FQ4 gross-margin guide below 48%, or a quantified App Store take-rate loss.

Stated gaps I am not papering over: there is no sentiment report in this run at all; the news sample is thin and confined to 29 September with duplicate layoff records and no 23–28 September flow; there is no segment, product or geographic detail behind the 16% revenue growth, so 50.06% margin durability is unattributable on either side; valuation is not computable from the filings, so 36–37x is illustrative off a cross-report EPS midpoint and is not a decisive input; there is no options chain or implied volatility, so the put/collar overlay cannot be priced here and event risk must be managed through gross exposure; and with no portfolio context every size is a fraction of the caller's own standard AAPL allocation, subject to their single-name limits. All cited levels are technical, not valuation-derived.

**Price Target**: 345.34

**Time Horizon**: 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4/FY2026 print

REFLECTION:
The five-day window gave +1.1% raw but -0.8% alpha versus SPY, so the Hold was acceptable in absolute terms but lagged the benchmark, and five days is too short to judge a 1–3 month, FQ4-gated thesis. It supports the bearish near-term entry/tape leg—AAPL was below the 10-EMA/VWMA and stayed a laggard—while neither validating nor undercutting the bull trend/fundamental leg because neither 339.50 nor 328.35/322.09 was tested. Next time, when price is below VWMA and the call is Hold with staged adds, benchmark the neutral stance against SPY explicitly and keep any probe smaller or deferred until a volume-confirmed reclaim, rather than reading absolute drift as confirmation.

**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Overweight AAPL — constructive on the franchise, patient on the price; do not pay the $329.40 quote. Build in three tranches: 25–30% of a standard allocation at $318–$322 (50 SMA $321.98), 30–35% at $315–$317 only if RSI actually resets into the low-to-mid 40s with stabilizing volume, and 20–25% on a volume-backed reclaim of $335 above ~42.5M shares — that last tranche must be a smaller risk unit or carry a tighter protective level, because $335 is over 8% above the $308 stop versus 4.3% from $322. The aggressive seat wins the fundamentals and the structure, and neither opponent laid a number against them: 9M FY2026 revenue +16.1% with Q3 +16.4%, Q3 gross margin 50.06% (+357 bps), diluted EPS +22.4% (Q3 +28.7%), operating cash flow +43.1%, FCF +52.5% at ~108.6% conversion of net income, net cash nearly doubled to ~$62.2B, debt −14.5%, $146.5B of liquidity, price 14.2% above a rising 200 SMA with the 50 SMA ($321.98) 11.7% above it. The $5.7B patent verdict is ~0.1% of market cap against $110B of nine-month FCF and is under appeal — not a thesis-killer. Critically, this is not the 09-21/09-22 setup: those trimmed into a $339–$345 resistance stack, whereas AAPL at $329.40 has already pulled back to 2.3% above the 50 SMA, so trimming here would be selling support rather than supply.

The bear wins the entry, and the aggressive seat overstates how much risk is "priced." AAPL sits below the 10 EMA ($334.77), below the VWMA ($333.99), below the Bollinger mid ($330.96), with a fresh negative MACD histogram (−0.283), stacked supply at $330.96/$333.99/$334.77/$337–338, and RSI at 50.9 with no oversold cushion — the trader's own plan calls $329.40 "no-man's land," a concession dispositive against paying spot. The conservative seat's gap arithmetic is unrebutted: a $308 stop gives 4.3% of room, but AAPL printed 6/25 and 7/31 gaps of −6% to −7% (the latter on 132.5M shares), so the stop defines intended loss, not worst-case. The 0.9x-volume decline (38.48M vs ~42.5M average) is symmetric evidence — sellers weren't aggressive, but neither were buyers — and supports patience, not a 40% first bite.

The decisive, unrebutted argument is the neutral seat's: substituting the full 40% tranche on a $335 reclaim is not the same risk unit as buying $322, since $335 to the $308 stop is over 8% versus 4.3%. Weighting 40% to the least-confirmed branch and 25% to the better-confirmed one inverts the ladder, so tranche one drops to 25–30% and any $335 entry must be smaller or tighter-stopped.

The conservative seat overreaches by capping pre-print exposure at 50% and making the confirmation path the only meaningful one — this desk's log shows gated adds placed below a rising tape (08-19, 08-26, 09-09, 09-16) simply never filling, and the 09-16 reflection required a market fallback committed at the same moment as the limit. Unresolved items that cap size rather than kill the call: FCF flattered by one-off working-capital swings (DSO +12 days, payables −19 days), the +91% net-intangibles and +32.6% other-noncurrent-liability jumps unexplained, opex (+21.9%) outgrowing revenue (+16.1%), buybacks −12%, and ~35–37x forward EPS on a record gross margin that prices in "peak is the new floor." Upgrade toward Buy on a volume-backed $335 reclaim (>42.5M shares) that holds its retest, or a Q4 print with gross margin ≥49.5%, converting inventory, double-digit revenue growth and reconciled intangibles. Downgrade toward Hold/Underweight on a weekly close below $309.90 ($308 execution), a failed reclaim of the $321.98 50 SMA with a still-negative histogram, a Q4 gross-margin guide below 48%, or an inventory write-down. Stated gaps: no segment/product revenue or margin data (so 50.06% durability is inference, not proof), no forward consensus or peer set to verify the multiple, no options chain or implied volatility to price a collar into the print, unresolved patent injunction/royalty details, and no portfolio context — every figure is a fraction of the caller's own standard AAPL allocation subject to their single-name limits, and all cited levels are technical, not valuation-derived.
